items.html:
Verified against current official documentation; no repository calls or mutations made. Let R=/repos/{owner}/{repo}. Current examples use X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-03-10.

Setting Enable/restore request Readback
Dependency graph and dependency alerts PUT R/vulnerability-alerts, no body; success 204 GET same: 204 enabled; 404 disabled
Dependabot security updates PUT R/automated-security-fixes, no body; success 204 GET same: 200, {"enabled":true,"paused":false}; 404 disabled
Immutable releases PUT R/immutable-releases, no body; success 204 GET same: 200, {"enabled":true,"enforced_by_owner":false}; 404 disabled

All writes above require repository Administration write permission. The alerts endpoint explicitly enables the dependency graph too; security_and_analysis.dependency_graph is not documented for repository PATCH. Repository API

Setting Request Readback
Retention PUT R/actions/permissions/artifact-and-log-retention with {"days":90}; success 204 GET same: days, maximum_allowed_days
Disabled Actions with selected policy PUT R/actions/permissions with {"enabled":false,"allowed_actions":"selected"} GET same: enabled, allowed_actions, optionally selected_actions_url, sha_pinning_required
Selected allowlist PUT R/actions/permissions/selected-actions with original github_owned_allowed, verified_allowed, patterns_allowed GET same returns those fields

The documented prerequisite for selected-actions GET/PUT is allowed_actions:"selected"; there is no documented enabled:true requirement. Consequently the disabled-plus-selected payload is schema-compatible, but runtime behavior while disabled remains unverified. Do not enable Actions solely to work around a failed request.

The docs also state patterns_allowed applies only to public repositories. Administration write/read permissions apply to these writes/readbacks. Actions permissions API
